# Go and Java names

The same concept under its Go and its Java name. Go names are in package `github.com/varveio/seekparquet/go` unless prefixed `write.` or `local.`; Java names are in package `io.varve.seekparquet` unless prefixed `storage.`.
A dash means the language has no counterpart. Names are checked against the code by `go/internal/tools/docgen`.

## Opening and closing

| Concept | Go | Java | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Open a local directory | `OpenDir` | `Dataset.open` |  |
| Open through custom storage | `OpenDataset` | `Dataset.open` | Java takes a storage.DatasetStorage. |
| Open options | `OpenOptions` | `OpenOptions` |  |
| Logical read policy | `ReadPolicy` | — | Go sets OpenOptions.Read for tail reads and speculation. Storage owns physical request execution, caching and observation. |
| Verify concurrency | — | `OpenOptions.verifyConcurrency` | Java bounds concurrent part checks during verify. Go uses an internal limit; the Source bounds physical concurrency. |
| Open statistics | `OpenOptions.OpenStats` | — | Go only; logical and format counters reset on entry and filled on every exit. Manifest reads are excluded from SourceReads and SourceBytes. The Dataset does not retain it. |
| Resource limits | `Limits` | `Limits` | Java builds them with Limits.builder(). See the limits reference. |
| Retained raw page-index cache budget | `Limits.PageIndexCacheMemory` | — | Go only; excludes footers and decoded indexes and does not bound overall metadata. |
| Check every part now | `Dataset.Verify` | `Dataset.verify` | Go: Verify(ctx, stats), with a *ReadStats or nil. Java: verify(ReadOptions). |
| Manifest metadata | `Dataset.Metadata` | `Dataset.manifest` |  |
| Dataset row total | — | `Dataset.rowCount` | In Go, sum PartInfo.Rows over Metadata().Parts. |
| A part's columns | `Dataset.Columns` | `Dataset.columns` |  |
| Close | `Dataset.Close` | `Dataset.close` |  |
| Supported version pairs | `SupportedVersions` | `FormatVersion` |  |

## Cursors

| Concept | Go | Java | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| A cursor | `Cursor` | `Cursor` | Java's Cursor is sealed: RowPosition or CommonPrefix. |
| Cursor after a row | `Row.Cursor` | `Row.cursor` |  |
| Cursor after a listing entry | `ListEntry.Cursor` | `ListEntry.cursor` |  |
| Next page of a range | — | `Query.next` | In Go, set Query.Cursor to the last row's Cursor(). |
| Next page of a listing | — | `ListQuery.next` | In Go, set ListQuery.Cursor to the last entry's Cursor(). |
| Cursor to token | `Cursor.Encode` | `Cursor.encode` |  |
| Token to cursor | `ParseCursor` | `Cursor.parse` |  |

## Statistics, cancellation and storage

| Concept | Go | Java | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Per-operation counters | `ReadStats` | `ReadStats` | Go fills a *ReadStats argument; Java passes a ReadStats to the consumer in ReadOptions. See the read statistics reference. |
| Batch and byte-reuse counters | `ReadStats.SourceBatches` | — | Source-batch, scalar-fallback, metadata-hit and memo-hit counters are Go only. Physical request metrics belong to storage. |
| Per-operation options | — | `ReadOptions` | Go takes a context.Context and a *ReadStats argument. |
| Cancellation | `context.Context` | `Cancellation` |  |
| Storage of a dataset root | `Source` | `storage.DatasetStorage` |  |
| An opened file | `SourceFile` | `storage.PartSource` |  |
| Bind reads to a context | `ContextBinder` | — | Java passes a Cancellation to every storage call. |
| Local storage | `OpenDir` | `storage.LocalStorage` |  |
| A part changed under the reader | `ErrObjectChanged` | `storage.PartChangedException` |  |

| Use after Close | `ErrClosed` | `IllegalStateException` |  |

| Base of the library's errors | — | `SeekParquetException` |  |
